page: Microsoft Azure E96-24as_v7 is a constrained-core, memory-optimized virtual machine within the Easv7 family, operated on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. It provides 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is extraordinarily high at 768.0 GB of RAM, corresponding to 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache architecture features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic primitives such as VAES and SHA-NI. The server includes no local storage or GPUs, requiring remote block storage.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate top-tier single-threaded performance alongside balanced multi-core execution. The single-core Geekbench score of 2890.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 3788.58 both place in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, complemented by high-tier single-threaded compression and decompression speeds. Due to core curtailment, multi-core benchmarks such as the multi-core stress-ng (45248.05) and PassMark CPU score (48197.74) align with middle-tier averages, whereas Geekbench multi-core registers strongly at 20290.0. Uncached read and write memory bandwidth achieve 102.85 GB/sec and 68.49 GB/sec respectively, supporting a strong PassMark memory score of 2834.41.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E96-24as_v7 is engineered for environments constrained by software licensing structures where licensing costs scale strictly per core. By restricting compute allocation to 24 vCPUs while granting access to the full 768.0 GB memory footprint of an enterprise 96-core chassis, the instance reduces database software licensing overhead while sustaining massive in-memory capacities.

The primary operational tradeoff is the total reliance on networked storage, as no local NVMe drives are bundled. Given the high memory-to-core ratio and robust single-thread performance, this server is suitable for enterprise in-memory databases, large cache layers such as Redis, relational databases requiring constrained licensing footprints, and extensive ETL pipelines.
